plain.text: The word of the LORD came to Abram in a vision: "Do not be afraid, Abram. I am your shield, your very great reward." Abram said, "Lord GOD, what can you give me, since I remain childless? A servant in my household will be my heir." The LORD said, "This man will not be your heir; a son from your own body will be." He took Abram outside: "Look up at the sky and count the stars, if you can. So shall your offspring be." Abram believed the LORD, and he credited it to him as righteousness. God said, "I am the LORD, who brought you out of Ur of the Chaldeans to give you this land."

Abram asked, "How can I know that I will possess it?" God told him to bring a heifer, a goat, a ram, a dove and a young pigeon. Abram cut the animals in two and arranged the halves opposite each other, as people did when making a solemn agreement. As the sun set, Abram fell into a deep sleep, and a thick and dreadful darkness came over him. God told him his descendants would be strangers in a land not their own, enslaved and mistreated for four hundred years, but God would judge that nation and they would come out with great possessions. Abram himself would die in peace at a good old age. When it was dark, a smoking firepot and a flaming torch passed between the pieces. On that day the LORD made a covenant with Abram, promising his descendants the land.

summary.bigIdea: Abram believes God's promise of countless descendants, and God seals the promise with a solemn covenant.
points: God tells Abram, "Do not be afraid, Abram. I am your shield."
"Abram believed the LORD, and it was credited to him as righteousness."
God makes a covenant, passing between the pieces as a smoking firepot and torch.
summary.reflection: God told Abram to look up and count the stars. When you look at the night sky, what promise could it remind you of?
